chunks: And Aban ibn Uthman narrated from al-Halabi: that he said,
To Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said: 'I mention the Imams (peace be upon them) in the prayer.' He said: 'Be concise with them.'

key_terms.أَبَانُ بْنُ عُثْمَانَ: Aban ibn Uthman, a prominent Shia narrator
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, title of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.أَجْمِلْهُمْ: Be concise with them / Keep it brief
key_terms.الْحَلَبِيِّ: Al-Halabi, a companion of the Imams

ai.seo_question: How should one mention the Imams during prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises al-Halabi to be concise (*agmal*) when mentioning the Imams in prayer, balancing reverence with brevity to avoid excessive length that might distract from the prayer's structure. This guidance reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *tawassul* (seeking intercession) through the Ahl al-Bayt while maintaining the ritual integrity of *salat*, ensuring that devotional acts remain focused and spiritually effective rather than burdensome.
